# Env Commands

Every command the `env` module offers, from its declarations, in order of the resource each acts on. Each command's help says the same.

## Approval

### `lnk env approval add`

Say yes, ahead of a run, to giving the environment file a secret it asks for

```usage
lnk env approval add <secret> --spec <spec>
```

It takes `secret`, position 1, string, required: The secret, by its name or its ID, secret:<id> (`lnk secret list`). It takes `--spec`, path, required: The environment file (env.toml) that asks for it. It answers `env.approval`.

### `lnk env approval list`

The secrets you've said yes to giving environment files

```usage
lnk env approval list [--json] [--spec <spec>]
```

It takes `--json`, boolean: Print the answer as JSON for other programs. It takes `--spec`, path: Only this environment file's. It answers `env.approvals`.

### `lnk env approval remove`

Take back a yes: the environment file's next run isn't given the secret without asking again

```usage
lnk env approval remove <secret> --spec <spec>
```

It takes `secret`, position 1, string, required: The secret, by its name or its ID, secret:<id> (`lnk secret list`). It takes `--spec`, path, required: The environment file (env.toml) that asks for it. It answers secret ID.

### `lnk env approval show`

Whether you've said yes to giving the environment file a secret

```usage
lnk env approval show <secret> [--json] --spec <spec>
```

- `--json`, boolean: Print the answer as JSON for other programs
- `secret`, position 1, string, required: The secret, by its name or its ID, secret:<id> (`lnk secret list`)
- `--spec`, path, required: The environment file (env.toml) that asks for it

It answers `env.found`.

## Env

### `lnk env check`

Read an environment file, its specifications and inputs, and print what it sets up and the hash its image is found by

```usage
lnk env check [--json] --spec <spec> [field flags]
```

It takes `--json`, boolean: Print the answer as JSON for other programs. It takes `--spec`, path, required: The environment file (env.toml). It reads the [`env` specification](../../../../config/specs/env.md), from a file or its field flags. It answers `env.checked`.

### `lnk env create`

Make a box as an environment says

```usage
lnk env create [--box <box>] --cloud <cloud> [--name <name>] --spec <spec> [--yes] [field flags]
```

- `--box`, path: The box file (box.toml) of the box made [default: the least that works]
- `--cloud`, string, required: The cloud account (`lnk cloud list`)
- `--name`, string: The box's name [default: the file's name and a number, app-1]
- `--spec`, path, required: The environment file (env.toml)
- `--yes`, boolean: Say yes to what it would ask

It reads the [`env` specification](../../../../config/specs/env.md), from a file or its field flags. It answers `env.made`.

### `lnk env reset`

Put a service back as the image had it, with its reset command

```usage
lnk env reset <service> [place] [--on <on>] [--spec <file>] [field flags]
```

- `--on`, string: The box (`lnk box list`) made from the environment
- `place`, position 2, string: A cloud account, or here: short for --cloud <cloud> or --here
- `service`, position 1, string, required: The service, as the file names it

It reads the [`env` specification](../../../../config/specs/env.md), from a file or its field flags. It answers `env.ended`.

### `lnk env setup`

Set a box or this machine up as an environment says, saving no image

```usage
lnk env setup [place] [--here] [--on <on>] --spec <spec> [--timeout <timeout>] [field flags]
```

- `--here`, boolean: Set this machine up
- `--on`, string: A box (`lnk box list`) to set up
- `place`, position 1, string: Here, short for --here
- `--spec`, path, required: The environment file (env.toml)
- `--timeout`, string, duration: How long it may run, as 30m or 2h; reaching it fails the setup [default: none, only each stage's own]

It reads the [`env` specification](../../../../config/specs/env.md), from a file or its field flags. It answers `env.ended`.

## Image

### `lnk env image create`

Build and save an environment's image now

```usage
lnk env image create [place] [--cloud <cloud>] [--here] --spec <spec> [--timeout <timeout>] [--yes] [field flags]
```

- `--cloud`, string: The cloud account to build it in (`lnk cloud list`), on a box made for it
- `--here`, boolean: On a box alone (`/etc/lnk/kind.toml`): the stages run here, for the computer that made it to save
- `place`, position 1, string: A cloud account, or here: short for --cloud <cloud> or --here
- `--spec`, path, required: The environment file (env.toml)
- `--timeout`, string, duration: How long the build on a box made for it may run, as 30m or 2h; reaching it fails the build [default: none, only each stage's own]
- `--yes`, boolean: Say yes to what it would ask

It reads the [`env` specification](../../../../config/specs/env.md), from a file or its field flags. It answers `env.ended`.
